messages.content: our CI/CD pipeline keeps breaking on flaky e2e tests

Quarantine the flakes — explicit allowlist of known-flaky tests that don't block merge but still run for visibility. Track them in a separate report. Then fix or delete them on a schedule (1-2/week), and if the flake rate doesn't drop after 3 cycles, that's a signal the underlying test infrastructure is the problem, not individual tests.

messages.content: our infra team is rolling out Kubernetes and I'm worried

What's the worry shape? K8s is good when (a) you have many services that need orchestrated rollouts, (b) you have ops capacity to actually run it, and (c) you have a real autoscaling need. K8s is overhead-heavy when you don't have those — adding it to a single-service deployment is a category mistake. Which side is your shop on?

messages.content: the AI we use at work keeps hallucinating dates

Common failure mode — LLMs don't have a clean way to refuse on temporal-uncertainty axes. Two fixes: (1) inject a current-date system instruction so the model has a fixed reference, (2) wire a retrieval step that grounds date claims in actual data sources. Don't trust an LLM to know what year it is or whether something is 'recent' without grounding.

messages.content: what's the right way to think about model evaluation at scale

Two layers: (1) automated regression tests — catch known failure modes deterministically, run on every checkpoint. (2) human-eyeball spot-checks on a curated probe set — catch the failures the regex doesn't. The trap is over-investing in (1) at the cost of (2); the regex grader is necessary but not sufficient. Build an explicit 'graders are noisy' caveat into your eval reports.
